subject: Recap + next steps: FinCentra pilot econ & ops
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@fincentra.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: FinCentra pilot econ & ops

Alice — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. High level summary below, followed by asks.

What we heard (pain points)
- Token spend is the biggest unknown: peak conversational volume is spiky (verification flows + customer support triage) and drives monthly volatility.
- Current model endpoints are expensive at scale; FinCentra needs predictable per-customer cost modeling to approve pilot spend.
- Latency sensitivity for verification flows (<250ms p95) — can't tolerate big batching-induced tail latency.

Goals you stated
- Run a 6-week technical pilot with production-like traffic (staging proxy of 200–400 reqs/min peak) to validate latency and unit economics.
- Achieve >30% token-cost reduction vs current baseline via batching/caching/quantization where acceptable while preserving accuracy of decisions.
- Deliver a transparent cost model that maps to your billing and ROI metrics for the 6-month roll-out case.

Cost levers we propose to explore in the pilot
- Continuous batching at request level for non-latency-critical paths (support summarization)
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated verification prompts (expected cache hit rate 20–35%)
- Model variants: float16 hosted variant for latency-critical flows; 8-bit quantized variant for high-throughput background tasks
- Autoscale policy tuned to your traffic SLOs to limit standing GPU capacity cost

Immediate asks / deliverables
1) We'll send an initial cost workbook and pilot scope doc (attached) — contains token-econ model and scenario slices.
2) You confirm two pilot personas and traffic targets (verification / support summarization) by EOD Wed (Oct 7).
3) Agree to a data access checklist (we'll share the minimal logs needed for cost telemetry).
4) Schedule a 30-min runbook review to confirm latency SLOs and rollback triggers — I'll send calendar options.

Notes on constraints you mentioned
- Budget guardrail: $40k–$60k committed for the pilot period, with review at week 3 for extension.
- Compliance note: logs need to be stored in your GCP project (we can do VPC/private deployment if required for production).

Attachments: redwood-cost-model-v1.xlsx (cost workbook), fincentra-pilot-scope.pdf (pilot milestones + ops checklist).

Thanks — I captured action owners below. If I've missed anything important, flag and I'll update.

Action owners
- Stephanie: deliver cost workbook + pilot scope (today, attached).
- Ben: propose initial infra config and latency-first deployment pattern (Tues).
- Marissa: draft the DPA/KM plan and minimal logs checklist (Wed).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Monroe <alice@fincentra.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinCentra Procurement <procurement@fincentra.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: FinCentra pilot econ & ops

Thanks for the clear write-up, Stephanie — super helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot personas confirmed: (1) Account verification (latency-critical) — target 250 p95; expected 60% of peak volume. (2) Support summarization (batch tolerant) — expected 40% of volume, can accept 1s avg additional latency.
- Traffic profile: baseline daily throughput 150k tokens/day, peak days up to 600k tokens/day during promos.
- Budget: pilot budget ceiling is $55k; procurement can stretch to $65k with clear ROI milestones at week 3.
- Compliance: prefer logs in our GCP bucket; will need a short security questionnaire filled (SOC 2 related) — procurement attached a template.

Requests:
1) Please include a 6-month ROI scenario in the workbook that shows net margin improvement for our verification flows at 25% and 35% token savings.
2) Can you provide a quick hosted vs dedicated cost delta for the pilot (we're leaning hosted but want to compare)?
3) Share a sample runbook for failover/backout if latency regression occurs.

I'll review the attached workbook today and get back with any redlines. Happy to chat Thu morning if that helps.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Head of Product — FinCentra

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 08:07:35 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap + next steps: FinCentra pilot econ & ops

Forwarding Alice's confirmation — couple quick notes from infra perspective:

On Thu, Oct 7, 2026 at 10:45 AM Alice Monroe <alice@fincentra.com> wrote:
> Please include a 6-month ROI scenario in the workbook...
>
Ben's notes: 
- Pilot config proposal (short): route latency-critical verification to an isolated float16 pool with reserved capacity to meet p95 SLO; route summarization to an autoscaled quantized pool with aggressive batching + KV cache.
- Estimated config cost (pilot week 1 steady-state): $6k/week float16 pool + $1.8k/week quantized autoscale (note: estimates pending validation in workbook).
- Risks: if cache hit-rate <12% then the ROI drops considerably; we'll include sensitivity table in the workbook.

I'll assemble the initial infra cost delta (hosted vs dedicated) and post a short note into the shared workbook by end of day.

-ben

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, FinCentra Procurement <procurement@fincentra.com>

Alice — appreciate the confirmation and the budget guardrail. Next concrete steps from our side:

1) Updated deliverables by EOD today (Oct 8): redwood-cost-model-v1.xlsx — now includes 6-month ROI scenarios at 25%/35% token savings, hosted vs dedicated delta, and a sensitivity table for cache hit rate.
2) Pilot scope doc (fincentra-pilot-scope.pdf) includes milestones, week-3 review gate, ops contacts, and rollback criteria.
3) Security questionnaire: Marissa will populate the SOC 2 checklist and return it to procurement by Wed (Oct 14).
4) Scheduling: here are 30-min slots — Thu 10/8 11:00–11:30 PT or Fri 10/9 09:00–09:30 PT; pick one and I'll send an invite.

If procurement wants a procurement-facing cost table (line items + payment terms) we can add that to the workbook; otherwise Ben and I will finalize the infra delta and expected weekly run rate.

Thanks — we aim to have the pilot pricing and runbook ready for the week-3 decision review.

Stephanie Nguyen

Redwood Inference
